title: Quick repeat shipments
q: A *quick repeat* is a shipment that comes 7 days or less after the same site's previous shipment. For every site with at least one quick repeat, show SiteID, SiteName, QuickRepeats (how many) and ShortestGapDays (the smallest gap in days between two of their consecutive shipments). Sort by QuickRepeats descending, then ShortestGapDays, then SiteID.
sql:
WITH e AS (
    SELECT SiteID,
           DATEDIFF(day, LAG(ShipDate) OVER (PARTITION BY SiteID ORDER BY ShipDate, ShipmentID), ShipDate) AS GapDays
    FROM oil.Shipments
)
SELECT p.SiteID, p.SiteName, COUNT(*) AS QuickRepeats, MIN(e.GapDays) AS ShortestGapDays
FROM e
JOIN oil.Sites AS p ON p.SiteID = e.SiteID
WHERE e.GapDays <= 7
GROUP BY p.SiteID, p.SiteName
ORDER BY QuickRepeats DESC, ShortestGapDays, p.SiteID;
how: LAG(ShipDate) OVER (PARTITION BY SiteID ORDER BY ShipDate) gives each row the previous date for the same site. Compute the gap in a CTE first: a window function cannot go in WHERE.
a:
**Approach hint:** LAG(ShipDate) OVER (PARTITION BY SiteID ORDER BY ShipDate) gives each row the previous date for the same site. Compute the gap in a CTE first: a window function cannot go in WHERE.

title: Median vs average shipment value
q: Averages hide outliers. For each ShipmentType, show ShipmentType, Shipments (how many shipments), AverageValue, MedianValue and AboveMedian (AverageValue minus MedianValue), all money values rounded to 2 decimals. Use the ShipmentValue column. Sort by ShipmentType.
sql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ShipmentType,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY ShipmentType) AS Shipments,
           AVG(ShipmentValue) OVER (PARTITION BY ShipmentType) AS AvgV,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ShipmentValue) OVER (PARTITION BY ShipmentType) AS MedV
    FROM oil.Shipments
)
SELECT ShipmentType, Shipments,
       CAST(AvgV AS decimal(12,2)) AS AverageValue,
       CAST(MedV AS decimal(12,2)) AS MedianValue,
       CAST(AvgV - MedV AS decimal(12,2)) AS AboveMedian
FROM m
ORDER BY ShipmentType;
how: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) returns the median on every row of the group; SELECT DISTINCT collapses it to one row per group. When the median is far below the average, a few large values pull the average up.
a:
**Approach hint:** PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) returns the median on every row of the group; SELECT DISTINCT collapses it to one row per group. When the median is far below the average, a few large values pull the average up.

title: Month-to-date running total
q: For Closed shipments only, show each ShipDate with DayTotal (the sum of ShipmentValue that day) and MonthToDate: the running total that starts again on the first day of each month. Sort by ShipDate.
sql:
WITH d AS (
    SELECT ShipDate, SUM(ShipmentValue) AS DayTotal
    FROM oil.Shipments
    WHERE Status = 'Closed'
    GROUP BY ShipDate
)
SELECT ShipDate, DayTotal,
       SUM(DayTotal) OVER (PARTITION BY YEAR(ShipDate), MONTH(ShipDate)
                           ORDER BY ShipDate ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS MonthToDate
FROM d
ORDER BY ShipDate;
how: Aggregate to one row per day first, then SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY year and month ORDER BY date). The PARTITION BY is what makes the total restart each month.

title: The sites behind half of all value
q: Rank sites by their total shipment value (all shipments). Show the smallest group of top sites that together make up at least 50% of the grand total: SiteID, SiteName, Total and CumulativePct (their running share of the grand total, 2 decimals). Break ties in Total by SiteID. Sort by Total descending, then SiteID.
sql:
WITH t AS (
    SELECT SiteID, SUM(ShipmentValue) AS Total
    FROM oil.Shipments
    GROUP BY SiteID
), r AS (
    SELECT SiteID, Total,
           SUM(Total) OVER (ORDER BY Total DESC, SiteID ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS Running,
           SUM(Total) OVER () AS Grand
    FROM t
)
SELECT r.SiteID, p.SiteName, r.Total, CAST(100.0 * r.Running / r.Grand AS decimal(5,2)) AS CumulativePct
FROM r
JOIN oil.Sites AS p ON p.SiteID = r.SiteID
WHERE r.Running - r.Total < 0.5 * r.Grand
ORDER BY r.Total DESC, r.SiteID;
how: Total per group, then a running SUM() OVER (ORDER BY Total DESC). Keep a row while the running total *before* it (Running minus Total) is still under half: that includes the row that crosses the line.
a:
**Approach hint:** Total per group, then a running SUM() OVER (ORDER BY Total DESC). Keep a row while the running total *before* it (Running minus Total) is still under half: that includes the row that crosses the line.

title: Longest monthly streak (gaps and islands)
q: For each site, find runs of consecutive calendar months that each have at least one shipment. Show every run of 3 or more months: SiteID, SiteName, StreakStart and StreakEnd (yyyy-MM) and Months. Sort by Months descending, then StreakStart, then SiteID.
sql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT SiteID, DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(ShipDate), MONTH(ShipDate), 1) AS MonthStart
    FROM oil.Shipments
), g AS (
    SELECT SiteID, MonthStart,
           DATEADD(month, -ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY SiteID ORDER BY MonthStart), MonthStart) AS Island
    FROM m
), r AS (
    SELECT SiteID, MIN(MonthStart) AS StreakStart, MAX(MonthStart) AS StreakEnd, COUNT(*) AS Months
    FROM g
    GROUP BY SiteID, Island
)
SELECT r.SiteID, p.SiteName, FORMAT(r.StreakStart, 'yyyy-MM') AS StreakStart,
       FORMAT(r.StreakEnd, 'yyyy-MM') AS StreakEnd, r.Months
FROM r
JOIN oil.Sites AS p ON p.SiteID = r.SiteID
WHERE r.Months >= 3
ORDER BY r.Months DESC, r.StreakStart, r.SiteID;
how: The classic gaps-and-islands trick: reduce dates to distinct months, then subtract ROW_NUMBER() months from each month. Consecutive months get the same result, so GROUP BY that value gives one row per streak.
a:
**Approach hint:** The classic gaps-and-islands trick: reduce dates to distinct months, then subtract ROW_NUMBER() months from each month. Consecutive months get the same result, so GROUP BY that value gives one row per streak.

title: What comes next? ShipmentType transitions
q: Put each site's shipments in date order (ties by ShipmentID). For every pair of consecutive shipments, the first one's ShipmentType is the From value and the next one's is the To value. Show FromShipmentType, ToShipmentType, Transitions (how many times) and PctOfFrom (share of all transitions that start from that From value, 2 decimals). Sort by FromShipmentType, then ToShipmentType.
sql:
WITH e AS (
    SELECT ShipmentType AS FromV,
           LEAD(ShipmentType) OVER (PARTITION BY SiteID ORDER BY ShipDate, ShipmentID) AS ToV
    FROM oil.Shipments
)
SELECT FromV AS FromShipmentType, ToV AS ToShipmentType, COUNT(*) AS Transitions,
       CAST(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY FromV) AS decimal(5,2)) AS PctOfFrom
FROM e
WHERE ToV IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY FromV, ToV
ORDER BY FromShipmentType, ToShipmentType;
how: LEAD() looks at the next row in the same partition. The last row per partition has no next value, so filter out the NULLs. SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) is a window over the grouped result: it gives the group total for the percentage.
a:
**Approach hint:** LEAD() looks at the next row in the same partition. The last row per partition has no next value, so filter out the NULLs. SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) is a window over the grouped result: it gives the group total for the percentage.

title: Month-over-month jumps per region
q: Total the ShipmentValue per Region (from Sites) and calendar month. Compare each month with the region's *previous calendar month* (if the region had nothing that month, there is nothing to compare). Show Region, Month (yyyy-MM), MonthTotal, PrevMonthTotal and GrowthPct (2 decimals) for every jump of 50% or more. Sort by GrowthPct descending, then Region, then Month.
sql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT p.Region, DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(e.ShipDate), MONTH(e.ShipDate), 1) AS MonthStart, SUM(e.ShipmentValue) AS MonthTotal
    FROM oil.Shipments AS e
    JOIN oil.Sites AS p ON p.SiteID = e.SiteID
    GROUP BY p.Region, DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(e.ShipDate), MONTH(e.ShipDate), 1)
), l AS (
    SELECT Region, MonthStart, MonthTotal,
           LAG(MonthTotal) OVER (PARTITION BY Region ORDER BY MonthStart) AS PrevMonthTotal,
           LAG(MonthStart) OVER (PARTITION BY Region ORDER BY MonthStart) AS PrevMonth
    FROM m
)
SELECT Region, FORMAT(MonthStart, 'yyyy-MM') AS Month, MonthTotal, PrevMonthTotal,
       CAST(100.0 * (MonthTotal - PrevMonthTotal) / PrevMonthTotal AS decimal(9,2)) AS GrowthPct
FROM l
WHERE PrevMonth = DATEADD(month, -1, MonthStart)
  AND MonthTotal >= PrevMonthTotal * 1.5
ORDER BY GrowthPct DESC, Region, Month;
how: LAG() returns the previous row, which is not always the previous calendar month. Bring back the previous month's date with a second LAG and check it equals DATEADD(month, -1, this month).
a:
**Approach hint:** LAG() returns the previous row, which is not always the previous calendar month. Bring back the previous month's date with a second LAG and check it equals DATEADD(month, -1, this month).

title: Climbers and fallers: H1 vs H2 rank
q: Rank sites by their total ShipmentValue in the first half of 2024 (January to June) and again in the second half (July to December), using RANK() with 1 = highest. Only include sites with shipments in both halves. Show SiteID, SiteName, H1Rank, H2Rank and Moved (H1Rank minus H2Rank, so positive means it climbed) for those that moved 10 or more places either way. Sort by Moved descending, then SiteID.
sql:
WITH h AS (
    SELECT SiteID,
           SUM(CASE WHEN ShipDate < '2024-07-01' THEN ShipmentValue END) AS H1,
           SUM(CASE WHEN ShipDate >= '2024-07-01' THEN ShipmentValue END) AS H2
    FROM oil.Shipments
    GROUP BY SiteID
), r AS (
    SELECT SiteID, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY H1 DESC) AS H1Rank, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY H2 DESC) AS H2Rank
    FROM h
    WHERE H1 IS NOT NULL AND H2 IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT r.SiteID, p.SiteName, r.H1Rank, r.H2Rank, r.H1Rank - r.H2Rank AS Moved
FROM r
JOIN oil.Sites AS p ON p.SiteID = r.SiteID
WHERE ABS(r.H1Rank - r.H2Rank) >= 10
ORDER BY Moved DESC, r.SiteID;
how: Pivot the two halves into columns with SUM(CASE ...) in one pass, filter to rows that have both, and only then rank. Ranking before the filter would give different rank numbers.

title: Three-product bundles
q: Take the 6 products with the most units shipped (ties broken by ProductID). List every bundle of 3 different products from those 6 with the bundle's catalog price (sum of the three PricePerUnit values). Show Product1, Product2, Product3 (in ProductID order within the bundle) and BundlePrice. Sort by BundlePrice descending, then Product1, Product2, Product3.
sql:
WITH top6 AS (
    SELECT TOP (6) p.ProductID, p.ProductName, p.PricePerUnit
    FROM oil.ShipmentItems AS i
    JOIN oil.Products AS p ON p.ProductID = i.ProductID
    GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName, p.PricePerUnit
    ORDER BY SUM(i.Quantity) DESC, p.ProductID
)
SELECT a.ProductName AS Product1, b.ProductName AS Product2, c.ProductName AS Product3,
       a.PricePerUnit + b.PricePerUnit + c.PricePerUnit AS BundlePrice
FROM top6 AS a
JOIN top6 AS b ON b.ProductID > a.ProductID
JOIN top6 AS c ON c.ProductID > b.ProductID
ORDER BY BundlePrice DESC, Product1, Product2, Product3;
how: Combinations come from a triple self-join with a < b < c on the ID: that lists each set of three exactly once (6 choose 3 = 20 rows).
a:

title: Each region's busiest carrier, ties included
q: For each site Region, find the carrier(s) that handled the most shipments there. Show Region, CarrierName, Shipments and ShareOfRegionPct (that carrier's shipments ÷ all shipments in the region × 100, 2 decimals). Keep ties. Sort by Region, then CarrierName.
sql:
WITH c AS (
    SELECT st.Region, ca.CarrierName, COUNT(*) AS Shipments,
           SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY st.Region) AS RegionTotal,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY st.Region ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rk
    FROM oil.Shipments AS s
    JOIN oil.Sites AS st ON st.SiteID = s.SiteID
    JOIN oil.Carriers AS ca ON ca.CarrierID = s.CarrierID
    GROUP BY st.Region, ca.CarrierID, ca.CarrierName
)
SELECT Region, CarrierName, Shipments, CAST(100.0 * Shipments / RegionTotal AS decimal(5,2)) AS ShareOfRegionPct
FROM c
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY Region, CarrierName;
how: Window functions run after GROUP BY, so RANK() OVER (... ORDER BY COUNT(*)) and SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (...) work in the same SELECT.
a:
**Approach hint:** Window functions run after GROUP BY, so RANK() OVER (... ORDER BY COUNT(*)) and SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (...) work in the same SELECT.
